failures.test_name: npm scripts > npm run build exits 0 and produces .next/
failures.failure_message: AssertionError: expected 1 to be +0 // Object.is equality (Next.js build fails type-check)
failures.failure_trace_trimmed:
Failed to compile.

src/app/teachers/[teacherId]/page.tsx
Type error: Page "src/app/teachers/[teacherId]/page.tsx" does not match the required types of a Next.js Page.
  "fetchTeacherProfileData" is not a valid Page export field.
failures.root_cause_hypothesis: Next.js page files may only export a default component plus a fixed set of allowed exports (metadata, generateMetadata, dynamic, revalidate, etc.). The coder exported a data-fetching helper `fetchTeacherProfileData` from page.tsx (line 7) so the test file could import and unit-test it. Next.js's type-checker rejects this at build time. The unit test currently imports the helper from the page module.
evidence: grep of page.tsx shows `export async function fetchTeacherProfileData` at line 7 alongside the `export default async function TeacherProfilePage`
Next.js build error: '"fetchTeacherProfileData" is not a valid Page export field.'
src/app/teachers/[teacherId]/__tests__/page.test.ts likely imports fetchTeacherProfileData from '../page' (this is what caused the coder to export it)
Vitest tests pass because vitest doesn't enforce Next.js page-export constraints — only `next build` does
failures.suggested_action: Extract `fetchTeacherProfileData` into a sibling module (e.g., `src/app/teachers/[teacherId]/_data.ts` — underscore prefix keeps Next.js from treating it as a route). Import it into both `page.tsx` (for rendering) and `__tests__/page.test.ts` (for testing). Do the equivalent extraction for any similar helper exported from `src/app/resources/[id]/page.tsx` if the resource-page test uses the same pattern. Re-run `npm run build` and `npm test` to confirm both pass.

recommendation: Dispatch coder for a fix pass with three concrete actions: (1) `npm install -D jsdom` to unblock the two component test files; (2) extract `fetchTeacherProfileData` (and any similar page-level helpers) into a non-route module such as `src/app/teachers/[teacherId]/_data.ts`, then update page.tsx and the page test to import from there — this resolves the Next.js build failure; (3) run `npm run format` to format the 5 new files. All four failures share a single dispatch and no test changes are required beyond updating the import path in the teacher page test (still owned by coder since tester's contract only specified behavior, not module path). Contract and tester work are sound — the download route, teachers page, and resources page tests all pass on their own merits.
